en.marketHeading: What is actually different about marketing in {city}
market: {city} has an unusual concentration of technical buyers. Between the universities, the software sector and the advanced manufacturing base, a lot of the people you would be pitching here can and will open the account and check what you told them. Marketing that relies on the client not looking closely does not last long in this region, which is one of the reasons I like working here.

It also changes what the work has to produce. A {city} technology company selling software on a long B2B cycle needs attribution that survives a six month sales process, not a report that credits the last click before a demo request. A local trade or clinic in the same region needs the opposite: fast, simple, cost per booked job. Those are different accounts entirely and the region contains both in unusual proportion.

The third thing is that {city} behaves as one market and three cities. Kitchener, Waterloo and Cambridge have separate identities and separate search behaviour, and Guelph sits close enough to blur the edge. Targeting the region as a single blob works for some businesses and wastes money for others, and it is worth deciding on purpose rather than by default.

For B2B here that usually means tracking through to a qualified opportunity rather than stopping at the click, because a lead count tells you almost nothing on a long cycle.

faq.q: Do you have an office in {city}?
faq.a: No. I am based in Toronto and work from home, so there is no {city} office and I am not going to imply there is. Everything is run remotely over video and email, which is how I run every account.

faq.q: We sell B2B software on a long cycle. Does Google Ads work for that?
faq.a: It can, and only if the measurement is built for it. If the account optimises to form fills you will get form fills and no pipeline. What has to happen is tracking that follows through to qualified opportunities and closed revenue, and enough patience to judge the account on a cycle rather than a month. If your sales cycle is nine months and you want a verdict in six weeks, no channel will give you an honest one.

faq.q: Will you show us the account?
faq.a: Yes, and I would rather you look. The account lives in your own Google Ads and Analytics properties, you own them, and I will walk you through what is in there whenever you want. If a vendor will not show you the account, that is the answer to a different question.

faq.q: Should we target Kitchener, Waterloo and Cambridge separately?
faq.a: It depends on whether your customers behave differently across the three, and often they do. A local service business usually should split them so you can see where the work is coming from. A technology company selling nationally should probably not be targeting the region at all beyond hiring and brand purposes.
Google Ads management is $1,500 a month plus your ad spend. SEO consulting is $1,200 a month. AIO consulting is $1,800 one time. No setup fees and no long contract.
